Metadata.title: AnyThingISee — Local disassembler and decompiler for Windows
Metadata.description: A free analysis tool to read x64 PE and ELF files as linked C pseudocode and assembly, keep names and notes, and export patches.

hero.eyebrow: Local disassembler and decompiler for Windows
hero.title:
Read what's behind the assembly,
right on your PC
hero.body: Open an x64 PE or ELF and get C pseudocode linked line by line to assembly. Keep names and notes, patch instructions and export them to a separate file. No separate Ghidra or Java install needed.
hero.visualLabel: Example of C pseudocode shown side by side with assembly

release.title: Free Edition 0.1.0 Preview
release.body: Our first public preview. Check important conditions, types and return values against the original assembly.
items: Built-in C decompiler with assembly, graph and data views
Function and data navigation, project notes

features.title: Every view you need, in one window
features.body: Open a file, pick a function, and the views move together.

items.title: C pseudocode ↔ assembly
items.body: Select a C line to see the instructions at the linked addresses.

items.title: Graph, data and byte views
items.body: Inspect the flow graph, data and file bytes for the same function.

items.title: Function and data navigation
items.body: Double-click a function name to jump to it, or a data name to see its bytes.

items.title: Project names and notes
items.body: Rename variables and functions and keep notes in a project.

items.title: Instruction patching
items.body: Edit instructions, review the changes and export them to a separate file.

items.title: EN · KO · JA interface
items.body: Switch language and display options in Settings; find shortcuts in Help.

steps.title: Open a file
steps.body: Choose a file or drop it onto the window. Opening a file never runs it.

steps.title: Pick a function
steps.body: Select a function on the left and read C and assembly together.

steps.title: Keep names and notes
steps.body: Create a project to keep renames and notes. Press F2 to rename.

steps.title: Export a patch
steps.body: Edit instructions and export the result to a separate file.

setup.title: One install and you're done
setup.body: No separate Ghidra or Java install. Everything it needs ships in the installer.

compare.title: See how it compares
compare.body: We measure analysis time, memory and install size against Ghidra, IDA Free, Binary Ninja Free and Cutter under the same conditions, and publish the results.

items.a: Yes. Individuals and organizations can use the current Free Edition at no cost, including for commercial work. A future paid edition will not retroactively charge for this free version.
The AnyThingISee source is not published. Bundled third-party components, such as the Ghidra native decompiler, keep their own licenses.

items.q: Windows shows a warning when I install.
items.a: The installer is not code-signed yet. Check the SHA-256 and the download source on the download page. You don't need to turn off any security features.

items.q: Can I trust the decompiler output?
items.a: This is a preview and complete recovery is not guaranteed for every binary. Verify types, conditions, call arguments and return values against the original assembly before relying on them.
Only Windows 10/11 x64 is supported today. A macOS (Apple Silicon) version is in development.
Open a GitHub issue with the product version, Windows version, steps to reproduce and the error. Don't attach private binaries or personal data.
